details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

AresNav (https://aresnav.vercel.app/) is a hyperlocalized, multi-layered Extra-Vehicular Activity (EVA) navigation and mission-planning system built for the first human explorers on Mars. While existing tools like JPL's Mars Trek are designed for regional and global planning, AresNav focuses on hyperlocalized surface excursions across four real Martian landing sites: Jezero Crater, Gale Crater (Mount Sharp), Arcadia Planitia, and Valles Marineris.

Astronauts can toggle four mission-critical NASA data layers—Topography & Slope (MRO HiRISE/MOLA), Surface Weather & Dust (InSight/MARCI), Space Radiation & Solar Alerts (Curiosity RAD & NASA DONKI), and Geologic/Ice Science Targets (Perseverance/Curiosity)—on an interactive tactical map. Users place custom Start Base (EVA-1) and Target Waypoints to compute three multi-objective routes (Safest, Fastest, and Max Science), inspect elevation and slope profiles, and monitor xEMU spacesuit life-support margins calibrated to Mars surface gravity (3.72076 m/s²).

KEY FEATURES & CREATIVITY:

- Multi-Objective AI Pathfinding & ARES-AI Copilot: Enforces a 25.0° spacesuit slope safety cutoff while calculating metabolic Oxygen (O₂) and battery consumption.

- Astronaut Helmet Visor HUD: Switches the interface into an xEMU helmet visor view displaying live suit pressure (4.3 PSI), heart rate, and metabolic expenditure.

- Autonomous Solar Storm Re-Routing: Simulates the ~14m 18s one-way (~28m 36s round-trip) Earth-to-Mars communication delay. When a live NASA DONKI solar flare or dust storm strikes, AresNav's onboard AI immediately overrides manual waiting and re-routes the astronaut and companion Scout Rover to the nearest safe shelter (such as Neretva Basalt Tube or Butler Plains Bunker).

- UHF Line-of-Sight (LOS) & Avionics Export: Detects terrain radio shadows behind crater rims and exports avionics-ready .JSON flight plans.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED:

- Frontend & Architecture: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons

- Visualization & Audio: Interactive HTML5 Canvas / SVG Tactical Map, Elevation Profiler, and Web Audio API Mission Control telemetry cues

- Data & Deployment: NASA Open APIs (DONKI), NASA PDS Planetary Constants, GitHub (MIT Open-Source License), and Vercel

INTENDED IMPACT:

AresNav bridges the gap between raw planetary datasets and real-time astronaut survival, providing a scalable, open-source navigation blueprint adaptable to future Mars surface missions and NASA's Lunar Artemis program.
